## Scheduled operator cycle, 2026-11-18 (~04:1x slot): closed the last named shallow-clone instance (gate_status_currency's commit-range miscount), then found a duplicate commit of my own mid-cycle and dropped it rather than ship it

**Did.** Attached clean: `fetch`, genuine `fetch --unshallow`, `checkout main`, `merge --ff-only`, no reset or force. Read `BACKLOG-2026-09-07.md` in full, `ROADMAP-2026-2029.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, and the last four `ops/NIGHTLY-LOG.md` entries before picking anything. `preflight.py --skip-tests` run live first: 0 FAIL, 31 warnings, all standing. 31 open GitHub issues re-pulled live: unchanged, all `decision`/`blocked-on-art`, none from Phil since #65 (confirmed directly via the API, not cited). `inbox_agent.py --apply`: no mail credential, standing gap.

**First attempt was a duplicate, caught before it shipped twice.** Picked up the 03:0x PM check-in's own handoff (harden `build_seo.py`'s `_committed_date()` and `check_cron_cadence.py`'s `last_changed()` against the shallow-boundary false-positive already fixed in `cold_read_ledger.py`) and fixed both independently. On push, found a concurrent 03:4x PM check-in had landed the identical fix minutes earlier (`3394d1a5b`). Compared both diffs directly rather than assume: same two functions, same guard, same shape. Rebased onto `origin/main` and used `git rebase --skip` on my own now-redundant commit instead of force-pushing over or duplicating the fix; verified the tree afterward carried their fix and none of mine, so nothing shipped twice.

**The real find this cycle.** That same PM check-in named a differently-shaped remaining risk: `gate_status_currency()` in `ops/preflight.py` resolves STATUS.md's last-edit commit via `git log -1 -- STATUS.md` with no boundary guard, then diffs that hash against HEAD to count material commits STATUS.md never mentioned. On a shallow clone, a boundary commit with no visible parent gets credited with touching every path in its own tree, so if STATUS.md was not really edited since before the boundary, "last" silently resolves to the boundary's own hash. Unlike the date-only instances, this miscounts a commit *range*: on a deep shallow clone it can overcount unrelated history as unmentioned material commits and warn falsely; on an exactly-HEAD boundary (the common depth-1 shape) it silently reports zero unmentioned commits, a false "current" verdict with nothing actually measured, the CLAUDE.md 0.4 shape ("unknown is not unused") rather than the "wrong date" shape the other four fixes caught.

**Verified, not assumed.** Confirmed the guard would have caught nothing by coincidence: a monkeypatch test using the *real* last-touch hash as the faked boundary produced no behavioural difference between old and new code (the real range from that point is only 2 unmentioned material commits, below threshold), so a naive fail-then-pass against real history would have proven nothing. Rebuilt the test with fully synthetic git plumbing (boundary resolution, a 9-commit unmentioned range, each commit touching a material path) and proved it fails against the unguarded gate (a real false warning fires) and passes once the guard lands. Re-grepped every remaining raw `git log -1 -- path` caller across `ops/*.py`: all are now either guarded (`cold_read_ledger.py`, `build_seo.py`, `check_cron_cadence.py`, `preflight.py`'s own `_last_commit_epoch`/`gate_status_currency`), refuse to run while shallow (`affiliate_report.py`), or are path-independent (`dashboard.py`'s bare `git log -1 --format=%s`, HEAD's own commit, immune by construction). `check_urls.py` (236/236), `audit_pages.py` (0 findings), `cold_read_ledger.py --stale` (0) all clean. `preflight.py --skip-tests` re-run live to full completion after commit: 0 FAIL, 32 warnings, all standing.

**Went well:** catching my own duplicate before pushing it, by comparing diffs rather than assuming a title match meant identical scope, and resolving it with `rebase --skip` rather than a destructive reset. Also: this cycle's own synthetic-plumbing test is a better fail-then-pass proof than the sibling fixes' real-hash monkeypatches, which (as shown above) can pass against unfixed code by coincidence when the real repository state does not happen to exercise the bug.

**Did not go well:** running the same handoff a concurrent session was already mid-flight on cost a full attempt's worth of work before the duplication was caught; neither cycle had a way to see the other was active.

**Changing next cycle:** none beyond what's already standing.

**Next:** no further named instance of this defect class remains; all raw `git log -1 -- path` callers are accounted for. 31 open `decision`/`blocked-on-art` GitHub issues, none from Phil since #65; issue #42's cadence question still open since 2026-11-14.

correct fix on top, skipping under `SIXS_UNDER_PREFLIGHT` the same way the
sibling `test_generator_ownership.py` already does for its own expensive

fixed. Both fixes merged cleanly, combined, and re-verified directly.

NEXT FOR THE OPERATOR: watch `deploy.yml`'s next run against current `main` and confirm it reaches a real VERDICT line (current, or a named `building`/`ready`/`failed`/`none` state) instead of `unknown`, because that is the one thing this slot's fix could not watch to completion before handing off.

Attached clean (fetch, unshallow, `checkout -B main origin/main`, `merge --ff-only`, 865 commits fast-forwarded, no reset/force), tree clean on arrival, matched `origin/main` at `a09eb7464`. Checked Step 2 directly: the prior cycle's handoff ("confirm run 817's re-trigger actually succeeds") was genuinely finished, re-verified against the Actions API, not cited: `publish-image.yml` run 818 (commit `59867f5f9`) completed `success` at 20:41:39Z.

While checking production freshness I watched `deploy.yml` run 427 fire live (triggered off that same success, for `main`'s tip by then, `a09eb7464`) and FAIL at 20:43:48Z, a real, current, customer-facing-adjacent signal, not a stale one: `VERDICT production is serving a DIFFERENT build ... image build for this commit: unknown ... could not ask GitHub what the image build is doing (no gh, no auth, or no network), so why production differs is UNCHECKED.` Pulled the job log directly rather than trusting the gate's summary. Root cause: `ops/deploy.py`'s `classify_publish()`/`_gh_runs()` shells out to `gh run list` to tell a benign registry-pull lag apart from a real stuck/failed image build, but `deploy.yml`'s job `permissions:` block granted only `contents: write` (no `actions: read`) and its `Deploy` step never exported `GITHUB_TOKEN`, so `gh` always had no auth and the classifier always fell into the uninformative `unknown` branch, on every mismatch, since this workflow was written. `checks.yml` already carries the exact working pattern for this repo's own `gh` usage (`permissions: actions: read` plus `GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}` on the step that calls it); mirrored both onto `deploy.yml`.

This does not make the current mismatch disappear (build-id lag between the image GHCR has and the commit `main` is now at is real, and `classify_publish` is correctly designed to still fail the job rather than guess), but it fixes the diagnosis so the next run says `building`/`ready`/`failed`/`none` with real advice instead of `unknown`, closing a gap that has silently made every past deploy-mismatch unresolvable from the log alone. `ops/tests/test_deploy_publish_state.py` (16/16, logic untouched, confirms this was pure wiring) and a YAML parse check both run directly. Full `preflight.py --skip-tests` would not finish inside this slot (same sandbox contention prior cycles logged); reported unchecked, not assumed passing.

`BACKLOG-2026-09-07.md` sections 2-6: nothing unstruck beyond Done/Hold/Phil-gated (A165 is the latest, Done). GitHub's 31 open issues re-pulled live: unchanged since #65, none from Phil since #64. No push notification: this is a mechanical CI diagnostic fix, not a new finding needing Phil's action, and the standing notification floor has not passed regardless.

**Did.** Attached clean: unshallowed, `checkout main`, `merge --ff-only` onto `origin/main` (459 commits, no reset/force). GitHub's 31 open issues re-pulled live: unchanged since 2026-11-08, all `decision`/`P0`/`blocked-on-art`, none from Phil. `inbox_agent.py --apply`: no mail credential, standing gap. Full `preflight.py --skip-tests` live to completion: 0 FAIL, 27 warnings, all standing. `room_guide_underperformance.py` re-run across all 20 rooms: 0 genuine on-topic `gap` rows anywhere, worst (Family Room, Garage) tied at 14% uncovered, matching `gate_room_guide_mining_diminishing_returns`'s own finding.

**Tried one partial-tier candidate and correctly declined it after verifying, not before.** Kids Bedroom's "how to organise daycare bag" (unmatched word "daycare", already routed to the right zone via an existing heading). Added "daycare bag" as a named phrase to `zone-also-called.json`, not the bare word, because bare "daycare" is the sole content word on a second, unrelated query ("daycare organization ideas"). Rebuilt and rescored live before trusting it: the heading still renders the bare token "daycare", so the scorer matched that unrelated query too, flipping it to a false "covered". Caught before shipping, fully reverted (`git status` clean against HEAD before committing). Lesson: a named phrase in this also-called mechanism does not avoid a bare-word collision, since the scorer tokenizes rendered heading text word by word.

**Reconfirmed, not re-attempted:** issue #65 (stale "Append" instruction in the Routines' own prompts) stays un-fixable by any agent session; `update_trigger` refuses on all three.

**Went well:** the live before/after diff caught a real false positive before it reached main.

**Did not go well:** nothing new.

**Did.** Attached clean: fetch, fetch --unshallow, checkout main, ff-only onto origin/main. Read CLAUDE.md, BACKLOG-2026-09-07.md (sections 0-7), the last several NIGHTLY-LOG.md entries. GitHub's 31 open issues re-pulled live via the API: unchanged since 2026-11-08, all decision/P0/blocked-on-art, none from Phil. inbox_agent.py --apply: no mail credential in this sandbox. All six rotators' own --check: CLEAN. preflight.py --skip-tests: every gate passed, 32 warnings, all standing. Mined the room-guide tier directly rather than cite "exhausted": confirmed live, every room between 4% and 14% uncovered on partial rows alone, 0 genuine gap rows anywhere, matching gate_room_guide_mining_diminishing_returns's own standing warning.

**Ran the full python ops/preflight.py (with gate_tests, not skipped) live in the background rather than defer it again, and it found a real FAIL.** test_audit_catalog.py: "the correct price $19 of 'The Whole House Print Pack' was reported as drift." Checked before believing it (CLAUDE.md 5d): the real catalogue audit was clean, 0 findings, so nothing was ever actually wrong with a live price. Root caused rather than re-run until green: an earlier background preflight run this same cycle had been killed by my own mistaken `timeout 110 ... &` wrapper mid-gate_tests, and test_audit_catalog.py's own "a wrong price must be caught" case had left site/_audit_catalog_fixture_<pid>.html behind stating a deliberately wrong $29 price for this exact SKU, because a SIGTERM skips that test's own finally-block cleanup. preflight.py's gate_no_stray_probe_files sweep, which would otherwise delete a dead-pid leftover like this one, runs before gate_tests in main()'s own ordering, so it cannot clean up a mess gate_tests makes later in the same pass. Reproduced standalone with no concurrent process running at all, ruling out a live-collision race before touching anything.

**Fixed at the root, not just the symptom.** audit_catalog.py's own pages() trusted every file matching its fixture naming convention under --include-fixtures, with no liveness check, so any bare invocation of the script or the test outside a full preflight.py run inherits a stale leftover from any earlier killed run, by any cause. Added the same os.kill(pid, 0) liveness check gate_no_stray_probe_files already uses, directly in audit_catalog.py's pages(), so a dead-pid fixture is ignored regardless of how the script is invoked. Fail-then-pass proved against the real file: planted a stray fixture with a confirmed-dead pid stating the same wrong price, watched pre-fix code report it as drift, confirmed post-fix code reports 0 findings. test_audit_catalog.py standalone now passes clean (ok, exit 0); py_compile clean. check_urls.py (236/236), affiliate.py --check (165 documents), check_sellable.py (124/126, 2 person-delivered services by design) all re-verified clean after. Removed both stray leftover fixtures this cycle's own mistakes had left behind (confirmed dead pid and untracked via git status before deleting either).

**Went well.** Ran the slow, often-deferred full test suite instead of stopping at --skip-tests, and it earned its keep immediately: it caught a real (if self-inflicted) defect class that a fast pass could never see. Verified the live catalogue directly before writing anything, so a transient test artifact was never mistaken for an actual pricing defect.

**Did not go well.** The stray fixture originated from my own earlier mistake in this same cycle (backgrounding a slow command behind a short timeout wrapper instead of the run_in_background mechanism, which then got killed). Caused the very defect class this cycle ended up fixing.

**Changing next cycle.** None beyond the fix already shipped; gate_no_stray_probe_files's sweep ordering relative to gate_tests is a known, now-documented limit (it cannot clean up gate_tests's own mess within the same pass), but audit_catalog.py no longer depends on that sweep to stay correct, so no further change is needed for this specific tool.

**Did.** Attached clean (145 commits). 31 open GitHub issues unchanged since 2026-11-08, none from Phil. No mail credential, unchecked. Production unreachable from this sandbox.

"next" joined FORMAT_WORDS; full two-corpus diff clean, 0 status changes, exactly 1 best_page change.

Second, and the one that matters: A125 had handed forward "the test_contact_form_interactive.py hang needs a per-test timeout in gate_tests." Checked first: the timeout already existed and was never the defect, so three cycles handed forward a fix already shipped. Real cause, measured by running it: this sandbox's Chromium starts, forks, then produces zero bytes of `--dump-dom` and never exits on a trivial page. `ops/browser.py`'s `find_browser()` answered from `os.path.exists` alone and called that browser usable, so 20+ browser-driven test files each committed to a 600s render that could not succeed. Fixed: `find_browser()` now proves the browser with one bounded 30s probe and returns None when it cannot render; callers already print "NOT VERIFIED" on None, so no test file needed editing.

**Verified.** `test_contact_form_interactive.py`: 600s-killed to 30s. Five other browser-driven tests now return in under a second, honestly NOT VERIFIED. New `gate_browser_probe_honest` fired with its measured reason. Fail-then-pass proved twice against real code (the pure function, and `find_browser()` itself). `test_keyword_demand.py` 71/71, `test_room_guide_candidates.py` 146/146, `check_urls.py` 236/236, `fix_dashes.py --check` 0/0, `affiliate.py --check` 165 docs, `check_sellable.py` 124/126, `link_graph_report.py` 0 orphans all clean. Live rescore matched the predicted 0 regressions exactly.

**Went well:** checking the handoff instead of executing it turned a fourth no-op cycle into the real root cause.

**Did not go well:** three cycles reported this correctly and acted on it wrongly (CLAUDE.md 0.2: a wrong cause, confidently repeated, costs as much as no report).

**Finishing it immediately earned its keep.** The complete run surfaced `test_cron_delivery_cadence.py` failing, then passing clean minutes later with nothing changed, the tell of an undeterministic test. Root cause: the case stubbed `delivery_gaps` but not the two other live GitHub Actions inputs its check also reads (`gaps_minutes`, `has_push_trigger`), so it claimed to test one seam while depending on two unstubbed live conditions, the same "checks something other than what it says" shape as the browser defect above. **Did:** Attached per Step 0 onto a shallow, detached checkout (fetch, real `git fetch --unshallow`, `checkout main` then `checkout -B main origin/main`, ff-only onto `0f19f52fd`, tree clean). GitHub: pulled all 31 open issues live myself, unchanged, all `decision`/`blocked-on-art`, newest still agent-filed #65 (2026-11-08), none from Phil since 2026-11-02. `BACKLOG-2026-09-07.md` sections 1b through 6 re-read line by line: every row Done, archived, or Phil-gated; section 6's owner-gate table unchanged.

**Found, traced, and declined a new keyword-routing bug.** Mining Garage's partial tier for anything genuinely closeable, "back of stove storage" stood out as attributed to `/articles/how-to-organize-a-garage.html`, which never mentions a stove. Traced it to the real mechanism, not assumed: `household_room_signal()` never recognizes appliance words like "stove" (it only knows room names and the household synonyms in `ops/room-also-called.json`), so this query's `room` field is empty, which disables the existing `_prefer_in_room_zone()` safety net (built 2026-11-05 for exactly this shape: a cross-room guide article winning by combining words from two unrelated headings) because that function requires a room signal to fire. The garage article's own "Put it back by how often it is used" heading supplies "back", and its unrelated "overhead and bulk storage" heading supplies "storage"; Kitchen's own Cooking Zone page genuinely discusses "the stove area" but never uses the word "storage" in a heading, so it scores lower (0.333 vs 0.667) despite being the real answer. Pulled every "stove" row in both keyword corpora (23 rows) to size it: most route correctly (Kitchen's Cooking Zone), a handful of low-rank long-tail rows route to unrelated room decks (primary-bedroom-deck, kids-bedroom-deck, guest-bedroom-deck) via the same generic-heading-combination shape, all scored `partial` or `gap`, never a false `covered`. **Declined to fix this cycle:** the clean fix needs either a new appliance-to-room signal dictionary (a new kind of file, not a small addition to an existing one, since `room-also-called.json`'s own documented methodology is specifically household alternate NAMES for a room, measured by query count, not objects inside it) or widening `_prefer_in_room_zone` with a materially larger, untested change; the actual cost of leaving it is a `best_page` pointer wrong on roughly 20 long-tail bing rows in an internal measurement file, never a customer-facing page and never a false `covered` claim. Building new signal infrastructure for that is the over-engineering CLAUDE.md's own section 0 asks this loop not to do. Recorded here as a real, checked, declined candidate (not a deferral written to avoid admitting "found nothing"), should a future cycle with a stronger reason to touch this file want it.

**Went well:** traced the actual mechanism before proposing a fix, rather than reaching for a quick patch (a one-off query/page override list keyword_demand.py has never used anywhere else), and sized the blast radius (23 rows, no false `covered`) before deciding it was not worth building for.

**Did not go well:** nothing new; same documented sandbox limits as every recent cycle. This is one more cycle in the run of "confirmed exhausted, nothing backlog-actionable outside Phil's gates" findings; the real constraint stays the 31 open owner decisions, several over a week old.

**Changing next cycle:** none. No push notification: the standing cooldown (no-repeat-before 2026-11-09T18:00Z) has not elapsed and nothing material changed (same 31 issues, same $0 this month, no new commit from Phil).

Added `ensure_pillow()` to `ops/preflight.py`, mirroring `ensure_pymupdf()`'s own retry/report shape exactly, and wired it into `bootstrap_fresh_sandbox()` alongside it. New `ops/tests/test_ensure_pillow.py` (4/4, same four cases as `test_ensure_pymupdf.py`: already-importable skips install, a failure that recovers on retry, a failure that never recovers reports False, attempts is honoured exactly). Fixed the regex. Fail-then-pass proved directly. Re-ran the live ranking before and after: Kitchen 39%->44% uncovered, Garage 36%->37%, both RISING because real demand that was always there became visible, the opposite of what "exhausted" should show after a fix.

Separately closed the original Garage finding: added "wall-mounted tool organizer" to the Hand Tool Wall and Cabinets zone (self-flattery checked, clean). Rebuilt. **Went well:** not trusting a fix's own "should work" story; the non-moving percentage after a supposedly-landed fix was the tell that led to a bug quietly undercutting dozens of "exhausted" findings across many days.

Attached clean (1336 commits). Previous work confirmed finished, re-derived: 29 GitHub issues unchanged since 2026-11-01, none from Phil since #42. `cold_read_ledger.py --stale`: 0. `room_guide_underperformance.py` re-run matches the prior handoff exactly.

**The real finding is self-inflicted, twice, both reported rather than swept.** Ran `preflight.py --skip-tests` under an external `timeout 280` picked without checking it against the gate's own internal budget (300s). Mine killed the whole process 20 seconds before the gate's own safe-resolution path could run; the already-spawned Etsy render kept going as an orphan, itself spawning an orphaned Chrome tree. Caught both before any committed PDF was touched, swept both process trees. Reran with no external timeout: clean, 33 warnings. That run then orphaned a second, different Chrome tree unprompted, which led to the real fix below.

**The real fix.** `gate_prerender_shop_current`'s own outer timeout (120s) was shorter than the inner timeout of the script it wraps (180s), backwards, so any real stall in that window guaranteed the outer wrapper would kill the inner script externally before its own cleanup could run, orphaning it with certainty. Raised the outer bound to 210s, the same margin the Etsy gate already keeps over its own inner budget. Does not fully close the gap: Chrome's crashpad can still escape a plain kill past 180 seconds, an accepted residual risk unchanged by this fix.

**Verified:** the gate's own test (5/5) passes, no orphan left behind, though it doesn't exercise the exact timing window this fix targets; said plainly rather than claimed fully proven. `fix_dashes.py --check` 0/0.

**Went well:** neither orphan reached a committed file; checked mtimes against git before killing anything both times.

**Did not go well:** picking an external timeout shorter than a gate's own documented internal budget is now a mistake this log has recorded twice in one day, by two different cycles including this one.

**Changing next cycle:** when wrapping a gate script in an external timeout, use a value comfortably above every internal timeout constant it declares; when in doubt, run with no external timeout and rely on the gate's own budgets.

**Next:** room-guide mining continues down the rank order, hours-scale work for later. Everything else remains the same 29 Phil-gated issues.

After pushing that fix, the stop hook reported an uncommitted change: `build/listings/etsy/L4-moving-in/listing-images/6S-Moving-In-Kit-1-first-page.png` showing as a binary diff from nothing to 364613 bytes. Investigated rather than discarded it (CLAUDE.md step 0.4, a file existing is not evidence of what produced it): `git show HEAD:<path> | wc -c` read 0, and `git ls-tree -l HEAD` confirmed the committed blob is the literal git empty-blob hash, while its two sibling images (`...-2-four-sheets.png`, `...-3-last-page.png`) are committed at their real sizes (454418 and 113848 bytes) and already matched the working tree exactly. One of three Etsy listing preview images for a real, soon-to-be-published product (`OWNER-ACTIONS.md` item 4, issue #44) has been a 0-byte blank file since commit `847beec22`, ironically titled "Fix gate_etsy_pdfs_current leaving preview PNGs dirty."

**Why nobody caught it.** `build/listings/check_etsy.py`'s listing-images check only ever counted directory entries (`len(os.listdir(images))`), so a 0-byte file counted exactly the same as a real photo, every run, forever. Worse: `gate_etsy_pdfs_current`'s own `_restore_etsy_all()` (added 2026-09-15 for exactly this file class) restores every touched file under `build/listings/etsy/` back to its committed state after each preflight run, which silently reverted any accidental real render of this file back to the broken 0-byte version, run after run, hiding the defect behind its own cleanup.

**How it actually got left on disk this time:** my own preflight2 run earlier this cycle stalled at `gate_etsy_pdfs_current` (documented network-bound stall) and I killed the parent process without noticing it had already forked a `build_etsy_assets.py` child subprocess mid-render; that orphaned child kept running for several more minutes and left this real render sitting uncommitted in the working tree once I later ran `build_etsy_assets.py` directly to regenerate it on purpose, briefly overlapping with the still-running orphan (caught via `ps aux`, both killed, confirmed no stray chromium/build_etsy_assets.py processes remained, then re-ran once, cleanly).

**Fixed both halves.** Verified the regenerated file (`PIL.Image.verify()`: valid PNG, 4167x3125, matching both siblings' dimensions) and committed its real content. Strengthened `check_etsy.py`'s listing-images check to open and verify every file, not just count them, failing by name on an empty or undecodable image. Fail-then-pass proved directly against the real file: zeroed it out, watched the new check fail with `"L4-moving-in has 1 listing image(s) that are broken: ...-1-first-page.png is empty"`, restored the real content, confirmed clean again.

**Verified:** `fix_dashes.py --check` 0/0. `py_compile` on `check_etsy.py`. `test_gate_etsy_listing_valid.py` (4/4), `test_check_etsy_free_duplicate.py` (6/6), `test_check_etsy_stale_economics.py` (5/5) all pass unaffected. Swept the whole repository for the same defect class (`git ls-tree -r -l HEAD`, filtered to zero-byte blobs excluding `.gitkeep`/`__init__.py`): this was the only one. Did not add a new isolated unit test for the image-validity check itself (the real-file fail-then-pass above is the strongest evidence available, and the check is already wired into `main()`, already called every preflight run via `gate_etsy_listing_valid`); a synthetic fixture test is reasonable future work if this class recurs.

**Went well:** treating a stop-hook's "uncommitted changes" notice as a lead to investigate, not a chore to clear with a blind commit; the file's own history and size told the real story in under two minutes.

**Did not go well:** running `build_etsy_assets.py` a second time without first confirming the first (orphaned) invocation had actually stopped, which could have corrupted output under concurrent writes to the same files. No corruption resulted (checked: all three images and the PDFs matched a clean single re-render), but the sequencing was sloppy; killing a parent process that may have spawned long-running children needs a `ps aux` check for that process's actual children, not just its own PID, before assuming it is gone.

**Changing next cycle:** when a backgrounded `preflight.py` run is killed mid-gate, check for orphaned subprocess children of that gate (`gate_etsy_pdfs_current` forks `build_etsy_assets.py`) before starting any new invocation of the same script.

**Next:** same as below. No price or product touched; one previously-broken listing image's real content committed, one check strengthened. `IndexNow` not applicable (not a site page).

**Did:** Attached per Step 0 (fetch, real unshallow from a shallow detached checkout, `checkout -B main origin/main`, ff-only onto `318cf15e7`, tree clean). Read `GOALS.md`, `BACKLOG-2026-09-07.md` sections 0-7, `ROADMAP-2026-2029.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, and this file's last four entries (entries 121, the Primary Bedroom fix; two PM check-ins re-confirming the 29-issue decision backlog unchanged; the Mudroom fix). `python ops/preflight.py --skip-tests` run fresh before touching anything: 0 FAIL through every gate reached. Pulled all 30 real partial rows from both keyword files directly, read each against real content. Most were the established noise classes (platform/audience names, generic modifiers, two digital-context "files" queries). One genuine gap, shared by two queries: "office supplies" and "home office supplies", missing only the plural word "supplies" against the Supply Cabinet zone's own singular-"supply" title, content-backed by its own purpose text.

**Checked for collision before shipping and found a real one.** Re-scored the full corpus after adding "office supplies" to `zone-also-called.json` and found "cabinet to organize cleaning supplies" (already diagnosed unfixable by an earlier cycle, "cabinet" names seven zones, left as an honest `partial`) had silently flipped to a false 1.0 "covered" claim. Traced the cause: `site/zones/home-office-the-supply-cabinet.html`'s "Cleaning it properly, surface by surface" heading is byte-identical across all 114 zone pages, so it was already contributing the word "cleaning" to every zone's heading-match signal regardless of actual content; adding "supplies" just tipped this one query over the edge. Fixed at the root in `ops/keyword_demand.py`: a `BOILERPLATE_HEADINGS` set (one proven phrase only, not a blanket strip) excluded from `page_inventory()`'s heading extraction. An earlier attempt this same cycle to drop every page's promotional cross-sell "band" section wholesale was tried against a full-corpus diff and reverted: that class of heading varies per room and often carries real zone-naming signal, unlike this one, which reads identically everywhere.

**Verified:** Added a regression test (`ops/tests/test_keyword_demand.py` case 21, a throwaway site tree) proving the filter keeps real title words while dropping the boilerplate; fail-then-pass proved directly, 26/26. `keyword_demand.py`/`keyword_demand_global.py --rescore`: both target queries moved to covered; the scorer fix also corrected several other previously-invisible false `covered` claims riding the same free "cleaning" word (a kitchen-properly query, six car/garage cleaning-supplies queries, two more), several now correctly redirected to Hall Closet's Cleaning Supply Zone instead of Garage; two diaper-disposal queries dropped from an undeserved `partial` to an honest `gap`, confirmed against the Nursery Changing Station's real headings, which never use the word "dispose". `check_also_called_digital_collision_fast.py`, `test_gate_also_called_no_digital_collision.py` (5/5), `test_gate_zone_also_called_is_heading.py` (6/6), `test_room_also_called.py` clean. `room_guide_underperformance.py --room "Home Office"`: 38% to 35% uncovered. `check_urls.py` (235/235), `audit_pages.py` (240/0), `fix_dashes.py`/`fix_dialect.py --check` (0/0), `affiliate.py --check` (165 documents), `link_graph_report.py` (0 orphans), `check_sellable.py` (124/126) all clean. `preflight.py --skip-tests` run fresh after, unbuffered to a file: 0 FAIL through every gate reached, genuinely stalled at the documented network-bound Stripe/GitHub-Actions gates (no `.env.secrets`), same standing sandbox limitation as every recent cycle.

**Went well:** running the full-corpus before/after diff instead of trusting a clean collision-checker run caught a real false "covered" claim before it shipped; following the cause instead of reverting turned one near-miss into a corpus-wide correction affecting more than a dozen queries.

**Did not go well:** the band-heading experiment tried and reverted this same cycle cost real time on a dead end; the lesson worth keeping is that a heading's wording VARYING per page is what makes it risky to touch, not whether it sits inside a promotional section.

**Changing next cycle:** `BOILERPLATE_HEADINGS` and its regression test are the gate this lesson earns. Other zone-template headings are also verified byte-identical corpus-wide ("Related reading", "Common items here" and others) but left alone until a second real collision is found, per CLAUDE.md's preference for a small reversible change over a speculative broad one.

**Next:** Home Office's remaining 28 partial rows are now individually diagnosed as established noise. Re-run the unscoped room ranking before picking the next room. Nothing from the 29 open issues is unblocked; no reply from Phil.

## Scheduled operator cycle, 2026-11-05 (~05:0x UTC): fixed the root cause behind most of the last two weeks' one-at-a-time "zone misattribution" fixes

**Did:** Attached clean. GitHub: 29 issues, all genuine owner gates, none from Phil, none unblocked. No mail credential.

Before mining another single-word synonym (the dominant shape of work for two weeks), checked a hunch instead: two rooms' remaining partial rows both confirmed genuinely exhausted, not reopened.

**Mining a different question instead of the same one again paid off.** Investigated why "master bedroom storage" was still scoring to a Kids Bedroom zone despite "master bedroom" already recorded as a measured Primary Bedroom synonym since 2026-10-02 and already rendering on the live page. Traced it to `score_rows()`: `best_page` was always set from the title-surface winner, even on rows where the heading surface scored higher and a different page earned the status. Checked the scope directly before writing a fix: 1402 of 2823 rows disagreed between the title-surface and heading-surface winner, 778 of those in a different ROOM entirely. Both downstream ranking tools read `best_page` as "the page this query actually routes to" by design, so every one of those 778 was a live risk of a future cycle "fixing" a misattribution by adding a dishonest also-called label to the wrong zone.

**Fixed at the root, not the symptom.** `score_rows()` now decides one winning surface before using it anywhere downstream, and breaks an exact tie between the two surfaces the same way the existing tie-break already breaks a tie within one surface: room signal wins, not whichever surface runs first in the code. The global corpus reuses the same functions, so one fix covers both.

**Verified:** two new test cases (a clean heading win, and the real cross-room-tie shape), fail-then-pass proved directly against the live bug's exact wrong URLs. Rescored both corpora: gap/partial/covered totals unchanged, exactly as expected since the fix corrects attribution, not scores. Spot-checked the regenerated report by eye: the named query now points at the correct page. All also-called/digital-collision gate tests, `test_room_also_called.py`, and the keyword-demand rescored-current gate tests all still pass. Full `preflight.py --skip-tests` to completion: every gate passed, 39 standing warnings, 0 FAIL.

**Went well:** checking why an already-measured synonym still wasn't working, instead of accepting "needs a content fix" at face value, found a tooling bug with 778 room-level misattributions behind it instead of one more content gap.

**Did not go well:** this bug has been live for over a month, during which some of the one-at-a-time misattribution fixes this log already recorded may have been chasing symptoms this fix would have prevented. Not re-auditing each individually: each was independently verified honest against real content at the time, so none are now known wrong, only possibly redundant.

**Changing next cycle:** none beyond the fix itself; this class of bug should not recur in a new shape.

**Next:** re-run the room-guide ranking across all 20 rooms with the corrected attribution before resuming the synonym-mining lane; several rooms' lists will have shifted. Nothing from the 29 open issues is unblocked.

No content, price or product page touched; a measurement-tool fix, IndexNow not applicable. Pushed to main.
